claims.text: P16: for a firm rules file claiming every protected wording (every v2 listed name and R21's director, capital, shareholder, lender, HMRC and returned-payment wording) for every category in every direction, no line a protected built-in pattern matches changes category or takes a firm: rule, under v1 and v2, with and without a case profile, in both directions; unprotected lines the same rules match do take them (positive control).

The case pipeline (overrides.case_figures, used by the workspace, preview and sign-off) loads firm_rules.yaml from the firm config and applies it: an unprotected credit and debit take firm:<id>, while HMRC, director, returned-payment and lender lines keep their table verdict; a per-line override still changes a protected line; editing or removing the file recategorises the case; a malformed file stops the case figures with FirmRulesError naming the line.

firm_rules.yaml format and validation (contracts): a mapping with one key, rules, each rule with id, pattern, direction, category, by, at, reason; refused naming the line for invalid YAML, unknown/missing/repeated keys, a rule id given twice, a reserved or malformed id, a pattern that is not text or has no letter or digit, an unknown direction or category, and a category the direction cannot take; a missing default file means no rules, a file firm.yaml names must exist; FirmRulesError is a RulesetError.
Lint passes over src and tests.
The full test suite passes with the change.

notes: Gap found and closed: under v1 (frozen, no rule marked protected) classify applied firm rules before v1's table, so a firm rule could reclassify HMRC, director, loan and returned-payment lines. New categorise._firm_rules_for withholds every firm rule from a line any protected built-in pattern matches (v2: rules marked protected with a category; v1: _v1_protected), so the line takes exactly what it would with no firm rules. With the guard replaced by an identity function, test_p16_no_protected_line_changes_category_through_any_firm_rule[v1] fails (mutation check run locally). Under v2 credit and debit paths already put protected verdicts first; the guard also covers a protected match set aside inside a longer unprotected phrase. Format choice: pattern is a counterparty name matched as a listed name is (whole words, separators; names_pattern), not a regex, so a firm rule cannot carry an exception, anchor or lookaround (R4); by/at/reason are required so every rule carries R20's record. overrides._categorise reads firm_rules.for_case() each time (memoised by file bytes) and the categorisation and bare-figure caches are keyed on the firm rules file hash; the pack snapshot already hashed the file (R22). cma run is not a case and is left unchanged. Promotion (R20's preview and save) is T37's and is not built here.
